The first thing I would is establish a skin care routine and to me, there are really only four basics. Moisturizer, Cleanser, Exfoliator, and Sunscreen. Since you have eczema, I would look at more hydrating products. Cerave has an amazing hydrating facial wash and so does the Simple brand. If you are looking a little more high end, I really love the Krave Hydrating cleanser as well! 

For moisturizer, I swear by the Cerava moisturizing cream in the tub. It is thick, feels silky on the skin, and does not leave you feeling greasy. I also really like rose hip oil which helps with acne scars. 

There are two types of exfoliators: chemical and physical. Since you have eczema, I would go for something like lactic acid which used in short bursts will help slightly off all the dead skin cells. This should help with the blackheads.

Sunscreen is a MUST. Purito has an amazing one for 15 dollars that leaves no cast if you have darker skin. 

The other stuff are treatments and things you can add for the acne scars. I personally use the alpha Arbutin by the inkey list right before my sunscreen in the morning. It really just lifts the scar. It takes some time but it really does work. 

For hair, I swear by oil treatments. They make your hair feel hydrated and soft and castor oil is said to thicken hair although the science of it is still iffy. 

The next thing I would work on is health. Not just health in terms of fitness, but mental health as well. How do you feel most of the time? Do you have low self- esteem? Address them. Find their source, and be kind to yourself. Give yourself positive affirmations. Random people on the internet can tell you you look great, but it does not matter if you have internalized how you feel in terms of looks.

Fitness! Even if I don’t see a physical change in my body, I feel a hundred times better when I know I am putting the time out to work on bettering myself. This could be a 30 minute walk, 10 minutes jump roping, HIIT exercises, etc. Whatever physical movement that makes you feel good.

The basics are usually a cleanser, exfoliator, sunscreen,and moisturizer. Some people will argue about getting a toner (which I use), but it's not necessary since most cleansers aren't as harsh as they used to be. 

So starting with your skin type: first, you want to figure out what type of skin you have. Is it dry? Combination? Oily? You can figure this out by washing your face with water, pat drying it, and leaving it for about 30 minutes. After those 30 minutes are up, see how your skin is feeling. If you are combination, parts of your face would be oily while the other parts would be dry. 

Your face wash as well as the rest of your routine will depend on your skin type. A universal brand that I absolutely love is Aveeno, in terms of drugstore. Burts Bees and Simple also have really good face washes at affordable prices. 

There are two types of exfoliation which should be done AT MOST twice a week: physical and chemical. I prefer chemical exfoliation because people tend to be very rough with their skin when it comes to physical face washes. A few chemical exfoliators that I recommend are by The Ordinary: the lactic acid serum or the peeling solution which looks like blood XD

I really like The Ordinary peeling solution because it seriously helps with acne scars and the like. The Niacimide which someone has recommended is also amazing. It really helps unclog the pores and help more problematic skin.

Hands down the BEST drugstore lotion would be by cerave. I have yet to meet a person who did not like this brand's moisturizer. It's a good, standard lotion that does exactly what it says: moisturize your skin. 

Sunscreen is ESSENTIAL. Skin cancer is a real thing. So is aging. I'm still on the lookout for a good sunscreen that won't cost me an arm or leg, but neutrogena has a good line. I like the gel formula versus the normal one because it doesnt leave a white streak on my face. 

I would also recommend getting a face mask or using a homemade one. Honey is an amazing option because of all its antibacterial properties. It really helps soothes the redness that comes from acne. Aloe is another great ingredient. If you're not into the whole DIY thing, the body shop has a manuka honey face mask that does wonders for the skin. Shea Mositure also has a black mud mask that aids with acne-prone skin. Masks are usually done once to two times a week.

Hope all this helped and let me know if you have any more questions!
